title: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) & LSTMs
description: Model sequential dependencies with hidden recurrence. Overcome vanishing gradients with LSTM and GRU gating mechanisms.

slides.title: Sequential Memory in Networks 🔁
slides.content:
# The Recurrent Hidden State

Standard feedforward networks assume all inputs are independent. Natural language, however, is inherently sequential—the meaning of a word depends on preceding words.

A **Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)** maintains an internal hidden state vector $\mathbf{h}_t$ acting as memory across time steps:

$$\mathbf{h}_t = \tanh(\mathbf{W}_{hh} \mathbf{h}_{t-1} + \mathbf{W}_{xh} \mathbf{x}_t + \mathbf{b}_h)$$

slides.title: Comparing Recurrent Architectures ⚖️
slides.content:
# Vanilla RNN vs LSTM vs GRU

| Architecture | State Memory Mechanism | Strengths | Vulnerabilities |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Vanilla RNN** | Single recurrent hidden vector $\mathbf{h}_t$ | Simple, fast execution | Vanishing/exploding gradients; cannot retain context past ~10 tokens |
| **LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory)**| Separate Cell State $\mathbf{C}_t$ + Forget, Input, Output Gates | Bridges long-range dependencies over 100+ steps | Higher parameter count; slow sequential execution |
| **GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit)** | Reset Gate + Update Gate (merges cell and hidden state) | Faster than LSTM with fewer parameters | Slightly less expressive on long complex sequences |

LSTMs preserve memory through a linear "highway" (the cell state $\mathbf{C}_t$) where gradients can flow without vanishing.

quizData.question: What is the specific role of the Forget Gate in an LSTM cell?

options.text: It erases the model's weights and resets them to zero
It decides what proportion of past information in the cell state should be discarded
It converts character tokens into byte tokens

quizData.explanation: The forget gate outputs values between 0.0 (completely discard) and 1.0 (completely retain) for each element in the cell state.

slides.title: An LSTM in PyTorch 🐍
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Sequence: batch=2, seq_len=5, embedding_dim=16
inputs = torch.randn(2, 5, 16)

lstm = nn.LSTM(input_size=16, hidden_size=32, batch_first=True)
out, (h_n, c_n) = lstm(inputs)

print('Output sequence shape:', out.shape) # (2, 5, 32)
print('Final hidden state shape:', h_n.shape) # (1, 2, 32)

slides.title: The Sequential Bottleneck ⚠️
slides.content:
## Why RNNs Were Replaced
Because RNNs compute step $t$ strictly after step $t-1$, **they cannot be parallelized across sequence length during training**.

Modern GPUs with thousands of parallel tensor cores sat idle while RNNs laboriously crawled word-by-word through text, limiting model sizes until Transformers broke the bottleneck!
